clue.text: One trapped in rugged MG after crash — he can handle extraction

indicators.note: the letter for one is shut up inside the other letters, as if caught in the wreck
a car crash leaves the letters of rugged and MG wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A driver is stuck in a battered MG sports car after an accident, and a rescuer is needed to pull them out.
explanation.walkthrough: A gum-digger is slang (originally Australian and New Zealand) for a dentist, the man who pulls teeth; extraction looks like a rescue from the crashed car.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists perform tooth extractions, and gum-digger is a jocular slang name for a dentist.

clue.text: Hotel, German, with a host unusually fine

indicators.note: used unusually, the letters of a host are set in a fresh order

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A German hotel where the landlord is remarkably pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to take Hotel, German as the definition, but German is only G; the definition is Hotel alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gasthof is the German word for an inn or small hotel, used in English for one in a German-speaking country.

clue.text: Matched pair trying to get on bandwagon?

definitions.text: Matched pair trying to get on bandwagon?

parts.words: Matched pair trying to get on bandwagon?
parts.note: the copycat's words make a matching pair with whatever was just said, and the phrase names the behaviour of someone jumping on a bandwagon

explanation.walkthrough: The two-word reply copies what someone else has just said, so speaker and copier form a matched pair; as an adjective it describes imitating whatever succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives me-too as an adjective for imitating a successful rival, which is exactly joining a bandwagon.

clue.text: Clumsy wife

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old disparaging English use of the nationality adjective for something awkward or heavy-handed
second meaning: Cockney slang for a wife, as in 'my old ...', short for duchess

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words look like an unkind description of someone's spouse, but they are two separate meanings of one word. 'My old Dutch' is Cockney slang (London working-class speech) for a man's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The nationality word once served in English as a slur for anything awkward, and as rhyming-style slang from duchess it names a spouse.

clue.text: Grass, ere cut, ensuring soft landings

indicators.note: the two words are cut up and their pieces reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Mowing the grass early so that anyone falling on the lawn lands softly.
explanation.walkthrough: In pilots' slang a greaser is a touchdown so smooth the wheels seem greased.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviators call a very smooth, gentle touchdown a greaser, so greasers are soft landings.

clue.text: Crude sugary stuff, right?

definitions.note: the whole clue describes the product: crude sugar is sticky goo, followed by the abbreviation for right

parts.note: goo is any sticky sweet substance

explanation.surface: Someone checking that raw, unrefined sweet stuff is what they have.
explanation.walkthrough: Goor (or gur) is the unrefined cane sugar of India; the sticky goo plus R gives the word and describes it at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Goor is a variant spelling of gur, the coarse unrefined sugar made in India from cane or palm sap.

clue.text: It's prescribed for ADD — some prefer it (a linctus)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run lying across them

parts.note: the answer lies across the end of prefer, all of it, and the start of a linctus, ignoring the brackets

explanation.surface: A doctor notes that a drug given for attention deficit disorder is preferred by some patients in syrup form.
explanation.walkthrough: ADD is attention deficit disorder, not addition; the brackets make (a linctus) look like an aside, but it carries the end of the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritalin is the brand name of methylphenidate, the stimulant most often prescribed for attention deficit disorder.

clue.text: Tea leaves in the bottom yielding faecal compound

indicators.note: the leaves are placed inside the bottom

parts.note: the sole is the bottom of a foot or shoe
kat (khat, qat) is the leaf of an Arabian shrub, chewed or brewed as Abyssinian tea

explanation.surface: Dregs of tea at the bottom of a cup that turn out to contain something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaves suggests dregs or the slang word for a thief, but here it is kat, the leaves of the khat shrub, once called Arabian tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Skatole is the crystalline organic compound largely responsible for the smell of excrement.

clue.text: Pa with 'Hers' apron? That's malfunctioning gland

indicators.note: something malfunctioning works out of order, so these letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: Dad wearing an apron labelled Hers, which is taken as a sign that something in his body has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranephros is an anatomical name for the adrenal or suprarenal gland, the gland lying beside the kidney.

clue.text: We'll introduce this major leap from Edinburgh for theatreland?

indicators.note: we comes in front of the answer, so taking it off the front of the whole leaves the answer

parts.note: London's theatre district is the West End
the clue's we, which will stand at the head

explanation.surface: Someone planning to bring a great Scottish leap of a show south to London's theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: Stend is a Scots word for a bound or great stride, hence from Edinburgh; put we before it and you get the West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Stend is a Scots word meaning to bound or stride, or a leap, fitting a big jump described as Scottish.

clue.text: I'll bow out of farewells between two (5, two words)

indicators.note: to bow out is to withdraw, so the letter leaves the word for farewells

parts.note: adieux is the French plural of adieu, goodbye
the clue's I, which will be the one leaving

explanation.surface: Someone excusing themselves from a round of goodbyes between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: A deux is French for of or for two, as in a dinner a deux; it is used in English for things shared by a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase a deux describes something done by two people together, especially intimately.

clue.text: Contraceptive? Opponent of it turned up in crowd moving rule on one

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed on another sits above it
the reversed word goes inside the crowd

parts.note: a drove is a herd or crowd of animals being driven along

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Pope is the most famous opponent of contraception
A as the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A contraceptive opposed by the Pope stirs up a crowd protesting against a ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a brand name; the it of the clue is the contraceptive itself, so its opponent is the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Depo-Provera is a brand of injectable hormonal contraceptive, given every three months.

clue.text: Lynx? Nonsense about lout with one

definitions.note: the caracal is often called the desert lynx, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the word for nonsense goes about, that is around, the other pieces

parts.note: rot means nonsense
an oik is a lout, a boorish person
A as the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Dismissing a boorish lout's claim that something is a lynx as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A rooikat (Afrikaans, red cat) is the caracal, a lynx-like wild cat; the question mark signals that it is not a true lynx.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooikat is the South African name for the caracal, the wild cat also known as the desert or Persian lynx.

clue.text: Put place for driving in Mediterranean vessel

parts.note: to set is to put
a golf tee is where you drive from

explanation.surface: Golf instruction about where to place the ball for a drive, set improbably on a Mediterranean boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessel is not a sofa: a settee is also a single-decked lateen-rigged sailing ship of the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the sofa, a settee is a lateen-rigged two-masted ship once used in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: One in murmuration starts to show temper at recent events

indicators.note: the starts, or opening letters, of the following words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words spell the answer

explanation.surface: Someone in a murmuring crowd begins to lose their temper about recent happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: A murmuration is the collective noun for starlings, and stare is a dialect word for a starling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stare is an old and dialect name for the starling, the bird that gathers in murmurations.

clue.text: Bum's wretched specimen seen from behind in transparent fabric

indicators.note: viewing from behind turns the letters back to front

parts.note: natal means of the buttocks (the nates), so it is the adjective for a bum's
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A grubby tramp spotted from the back wearing see-through cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal here has nothing to do with birth: it comes from nates, the buttocks, so it describes a bum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarlatan is an open-weave, almost transparent muslin, stiffened and used for ballet skirts and costumes.

clue.text: Curfuffle petty criminal tolerated without matching tails

indicators.note: without signals going without, dropping, the last letter of the criminal's word

parts.note: a hood is a small-time gangster

indicators.note: the tolerated word loses the same tail letter, so the two endings match and both go

parts.note: had, as in would not have it, means tolerated

explanation.surface: A fuss over a small-time crook who was put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words end in D; dropping that shared tail from each and joining what is left gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Curfuffle is a Scots word for a commotion or fuss, and a hoo-ha is a noisy fuss.

clue.text: Treat as irredeemable a cope's fastening holding it up

indicators.note: the fastening holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a morse is the ornamental clasp that fastens a cope, a priest's cloak

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A priest's cloak clasp is held up as unrepairable.
explanation.walkthrough: A cope is a long ecclesiastical cloak and a morse its clasp. To amortise once meant to alienate land in mortmain, so it could never be redeemed.
explanation.definitionFit: Amortise originally meant to transfer property in mortmain, putting it beyond redemption, as well as to extinguish a debt.

clue.text: Left restricted by union — fair

indicators.note: the letter is confined within the word for union

parts.note: a bond is a union or tie

explanation.surface: A political note: the Left constrained by a trade union is behaving fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair suggests just or reasonable in the surface, but here it means light-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light-coloured, and blond describes light or yellowish hair or a person who has it.

clue.text: Ring held by heavy headed pin that is forming US neckwear (7, two words)

indicators.note: the ring is held inside the pin's letters

parts.note: a bolt is a heavy metal pin with a head
O is ring-shaped
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ring caught on a big-headed pin turning into an American string tie.
explanation.walkthrough: A bolo tie is the Western cord tie with an ornamental slide, worn in the south-western United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolo tie is a cord necktie with a decorative clasp, the official state neckwear of Arizona.

clue.text: Maker of padded stuff fairly runs to bag end of roll

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the outer letters take in the extra one

parts.note: quite means fairly, to some extent

indicators.note: only the end, or last letter, of roll is used

parts.note: the end of roll is its last letter, L

explanation.surface: Someone running to fetch the last of a roll of wadding for upholstery.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilter makes quilts, padded bedcovers made of layers of cloth stitched over wadding.

clue.text: Once spattered with mud and bile, demo dispersed

definitions.note: once marks a word now obsolete, here Spenser's

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are scattered and regathered in a new order

explanation.surface: Protesters at a broken-up demonstration got covered in mud and bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: Once warns that the word is archaic: bemoiled is Shakespeare's word for bemired.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemoiled is an archaic word meaning bedraggled with mud, from moil, to wet or soil.

clue.text: Boy rod thrashed will curb ultimate in disruptive doings

indicators.note: the anagram letters restrain, that is enclose, the extra letter
beaten about, the letters are shaken into a new order
the ultimate, or last, letter of disruptive

parts.note: the ultimate letter of disruptive is E

explanation.surface: A disruptive boy is restrained with a beating from a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: Doings here is the slang noun for a thingummy, a whatsit, not deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Doobrey is British slang for a thingummy, an object whose name escapes you, as is doings.

clue.text: A couple of boundaries dismantled over-fancy stuff

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are taken apart and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: in cricket a boundary scores four, so two boundaries are four and four

explanation.surface: Fussy decorations taken down from a couple of fences.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a hit to the edge of the field, scoring four runs, so two of them give the letters of four twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou means excessively fussy decoration or frills, originally the rustle of silk skirts.

clue.text: Garda policeman nicks one backsliding

indicators.note: sliding back, the letters are read in reverse
to nick is to arrest, so the policeman takes the letter into custody

parts.note: slop is back slang for police, a policeman
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Irish policeman arrests someone who has relapsed into crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garda is the Irish police force; polis is the Scots and Irish word for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Polis is the Scots and Irish pronunciation-spelling of police, and the Garda is the Irish police.

clue.text: Like soft food for the old man

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... describes food like pap, soft and mushy
second meaning: an affectionate American word for father

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as soft food for an elderly man, but the two halves are separate meanings: an adjective from pap and a pet name for dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pap is soft mushy food, so pappy food resembles it; pappy is also a familiar term for one's father.

clue.text: Party beside ring for wrestling tournament

indicators.note: the ring letter is set next to the party word

parts.note: a bash is a party
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A party held next to the ring for a wrestling contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring suggests the wrestlers' arena, but it is only the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A basho is an official sumo wrestling tournament in Japan, six of which are held each year.

clue.text: Empty seat, first (second) vacated

indicators.note: it is the first letter of the seat word that goes
a seat vacated is left empty, so its letter leaves

parts.note: a saddle is a rider's seat
S is the abbreviation for second, and it is also the first letter here

explanation.surface: An empty seat that its first occupant left a second ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets explain that the first letter vacated is S, which is the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Addle can mean empty or barren, as in an addle egg that will not hatch or an addled, empty head.

clue.text: Jock's slight, also misshapen and short

definitions.note: Jock is the crossword label for a Scot, marking a Scots word

indicators.note: a misshapen word has its letters bent out of their usual order

parts.note: 'n' is the shortened form of and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's insult: you are also deformed and stunted.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock's marks a Scots word: sloan is Scots for a snub or reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloan is a Scots word for a snub or rebuff, so a slight in the Scottish vocabulary.

clue.text: At pleasure, getting on in afternoon dances (8, two words)

parts.note: A for afternoon, from the abbreviation of ante meridiem's companion forms

indicators.note: the word on is put inside the dances

parts.note: voltes, singular volte (volta), are a lively old dance; volte is the plural

explanation.surface: Ageing couples happily going to afternoon tea dances.
explanation.walkthrough: The volta (plural volte) was a lively Renaissance couple dance with high leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A volonte is French for at will, used in music and elsewhere to mean as one pleases.

clue.text: E. Indian tree — this alias is misused in Melanesia

indicators.note: the letters of Melanesia are used wrongly, rearranged around the named letters

explanation.surface: A note that an East Indian tree goes by a different, misapplied name in Melanesia.
explanation.walkthrough: This refers to the answer: it and the word alias together make an anagram of Melanesia.
explanation.definitionFit: The neem is the margosa, an Indian tree of the mahogany family valued for its oil and medicinal bark.

clue.text: Bird abandoning chaps for first-former?

definitions.note: a petty is a pupil at a petty school, the lowest class, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the bird name leaves behind the word chaps

parts.note: pettychaps is an old name for the garden warbler

explanation.surface: A girl dumping the boys to join the first form.
explanation.walkthrough: Pettychaps is a dialect name for the garden warbler. A petty school was an elementary school for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty was a young pupil at a petty school, the elementary class, so a junior beginner like a first-former.

clue.text: At home held by Hindoo rajah

indicators.note: the answer is held within the following two words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Hindoo and the first letter of rajah

explanation.surface: An Indian prince keeping someone captive in his palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Hindoo is the old spelling of Hindu, needed for the letters to lie across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor describes something done inside the house, and at home also means indoors, inside one's dwelling.

clue.text: Tests minister endlessly about English version (of Bible)

indicators.note: the shortened minister goes around the other letters
without its end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
V is the abbreviation for version, as in RV, the Revised Version

explanation.surface: A clergyman examines different English translations of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Prieve is a Scots and Spenserian form of prove, in its old sense of test or try.
explanation.definitionFit: Prieves is a Scots form of proves, meaning tests or tries, as in the proof of the pudding.

clue.text: Trainee in HQ, indifferent to pleasure

indicators.note: the learner letter goes inside the headquarters word

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
L for learner, from the L-plate shown by learner drivers

explanation.surface: A recruit at headquarters who shows no enthusiasm for enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plate a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blase is unimpressed by pleasure through over-familiarity, bored by what excites others.

clue.text: Historical tribute? More awkward with 'author, name unknown'

indicators.note: awkward implies the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: a pen is a writer, as in a hired pen
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A historical tribute made clumsier by being by an anonymous author.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome-penny was the annual tax paid by English households to the Pope, also called Peter's pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rome-penny was a medieval tax of a penny per household sent to the papacy, an old tribute.
